key_insight: Discrete Model-Based Diffusion enables training-free combinatorial optimization directly over discrete variables using denoising diffusion.
engineering_relevance: It offers a promising route to lower-cost optimization for time-sensitive multi-robot task allocation, coalition formation, and scheduling.
method: Integrates discrete denoising diffusion into sampling-based optimization.
Uses Monte Carlo sampling to approximate categorical reverse transition distributions.
Establishes a finite-step lower bound on global-optimum discovery probability that approaches one as denoising steps increase.
evidence_signal: Experiments on generic integer programs and heterogeneous multi-robot coalition formation and scheduling outperform sampling-based baselines in nearly all tested settings, with solution quality competitive with mixed-integer programming and reinforcement learning at a fraction of their computational cost.
watch_item: The asymptotic probability guarantee does not establish practical runtime; Monte Carlo sampling and denoising-step budgets must be assessed for deployment.
paper_title: Discrete Model-Based Diffusion for Combinatorial Optimization in Multi-Robot Task Allocation
